title: Speaking Part 1 — one question, one card
note: Chapters of five questions; each question has three answers at B2 — Default, Alternative 1, Alternative 2 — that differ in angle and shape, not level. Each answer is stored once in speaking order, with a 'frame': the answer reduced to its reusable skeleton. Answers land at 15–20 s (2.5 words/s); build3.py checks.
tip: Don't memorise answers. Memorise frames — then fill them with your own life.

x.name: React
x.hint: how the question makes you feel, before you answer it
x.ask: Now put a reaction in front — how does the question make you feel?

a.name: Answer
a.hint: say it straight, in one go

r.name: Reason
r.hint: why — the part the examiner could never guess

e.name: Example
e.hint: one real moment: a day, a place, a person
e.ask: Now prove it with one real moment.

c.name: Contrast
c.hint: the 'but' — the other side that makes it sound real

cards.question: Where are you from?

alts.frame: I'm from ___, and I've lived here my whole life. I really love it, mainly because ___ — and ___. Most evenings ___.
alts.why: A simple question, a simple shape: say it, say why, then one picture of your life there.

segs.t: I'm from Funchal, and I've lived here my whole life.
I really love it, mainly because it feels safe and relaxed — and the weather's amazing almost all year round.

wrong.t: I'm from Funchal, which is the capital of Madeira.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: Funchal is a city with approximately 100,000 inhabitants.
wrong.why: A fact from Wikipedia, not a reason. The examiner wants why YOU like it.

segs.t: Most evenings my friends and I sit on the wall by the marina and watch the cruise ships leave.

wrong.t: For example, Funchal has lots of nice places.
wrong.why: Vague. One place, one habit, one picture.

wrong.t: Many cruise ships visit Funchal every year.
wrong.why: A statistic in disguise. What do YOU do?

alts.frame: Well, it's a bit complicated, actually. I was born in ___, but ___ when I was ___. So I'd say I'm from ___ now — although ___!
alts.why: A 'complicated' answer is a gift in Part 1: the contrast at the end shows you can hold two ideas at once.

segs.t: Well, it's a bit complicated, actually.

wrong.t: That is an interesting question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

wrong.t: I am from Venezuela and Madeira.
wrong.why: That's the answer, and it skips the reaction. Show the question made you think first.

segs.t: I was born in Venezuela, but my family moved back to Madeira when I was five.
So I'd say I'm from Funchal now — although when my grandma makes arepas, I feel totally Venezuelan!

wrong.t: So I'm from Funchal and I like it very much.
wrong.why: No turn. 'Although' should swing back to the other side of you.

wrong.t: However, many Madeirans emigrated to Venezuela in the past.
wrong.why: History lesson. The contrast should be about you, not the island.

alts.frame: I'm from ___, a ___ just outside ___. It's the kind of place where ___. Last week ___, and ___!
alts.why: No reaction, straight in — then one tiny story proves the 'everyone knows you' idea instead of just saying it.

segs.t: I'm from Câmara de Lobos, a fishing town just outside Funchal.
It's the kind of place where everyone knows you. Last week I forgot my wallet at the bakery, and the owner just told my mum when she walked past!
marks: It's the kind of place where

wrong.t: For example, it has many restaurants and shops.
wrong.why: A list, not a moment. What happened, to you, once?

wrong.t: It is famous because Winston Churchill painted there.
wrong.why: True, and interesting — but it's a guidebook fact, not your example.

cards.question: What's your home like?

alts.frame: We live in a ___ in ___, on the ___ floor, so we've got ___. The only downside is that ___, which drives me crazy.
alts.why: Describe it, then complain a little. A small 'but' makes a description sound like a real opinion.

segs.t: We live in a flat in São Martinho, on the fourth floor, so we've got a great view of the sea.
The only downside is that it's quite small, so I have to share a room with my little brother, which drives me crazy.

wrong.t: Also, it has two bathrooms and a kitchen.
wrong.why: 'Also' adds another fact. A contrast turns the other way.

wrong.t: Nevertheless, the apartment presents certain disadvantages.
wrong.why: Correct English, but it sounds like a letter to the council. Part 1 is a chat — sound like you.

alts.frame: Oh, it's pretty ___, to be honest. It's my ___' house up in ___, with ___. It's ___ in winter, but I wouldn't swap it for ___.
alts.why: The reaction warns the examiner there's a story. 'I wouldn't swap it' shows affection without saying 'I love it'.

segs.t: Oh, it's pretty old, to be honest.

wrong.t: My house is an old house.
wrong.why: Flat and repetitive. React with a feeling, not a label.

wrong.t: Well, that's a good question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: It's my grandparents' house up in Santo António, with a big garden full of banana trees and chickens.
It's freezing in winter, but I wouldn't swap it for a modern flat.

wrong.t: It's freezing in winter, and it's also very old.
wrong.why: Two complaints in a row. The 'but' needs to swing back to what you love.

wrong.t: In contrast, modern flats have central heating.
wrong.why: About flats in general, not about your home.

alts.frame: It's a ___ house, nothing special, but ___ is my favourite place in the world. It's the only place where I can ___. Last month ___, and ___!
alts.why: 'Nothing special, but…' is a lovely move: lower expectations, then surprise. The example makes it funny.

segs.t: It's a normal house, nothing special, but my bedroom is my favourite place in the world.
It's the only place where I can shut the door, put my music on and just be myself.

wrong.t: My bedroom is my favourite room in the house.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: Bedrooms are important for teenagers' mental health.
wrong.why: A magazine headline. Say why it matters to you.

segs.t: Last month I painted one wall dark blue, and my mum still hasn't forgiven me.

wrong.t: For example, I have a bed and a desk.
wrong.why: An inventory, not a moment.

wrong.t: I like the colour blue very much.
wrong.why: A preference, not an example. What happened?

cards.question: Who are you most like in your family?

alts.frame: I'm definitely most like my ___. We both love ___, and we can ___ for hours. Last summer we ___. The big difference is that she's ___, and I'm… well, not!
alts.why: Answer, one shared moment, then the difference. The joke at the end is the contrast.

segs.t: I'm definitely most like my mum. We both love being outside, and we can chat for hours.
Last summer we did a levada walk together and talked the entire way.

wrong.t: For example, we are both very similar.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: Levadas are irrigation channels built centuries ago.
wrong.why: A guidebook fact. The example is what you two did.

segs.t: The big difference is that she's really patient, and I'm… well, not!

wrong.t: And she's also really kind and friendly.
wrong.why: More similarities. The contrast has to show a difference.

wrong.t: However, personality is influenced by many factors.
wrong.why: Correct English, but it sounds like a letter to the council. Part 1 is a chat — sound like you.

alts.frame: Ha — everyone says my ___, and it's so annoying. We've got the same ___, the same ___ and the same ___. Mind you, if I'm honest, I'd rather be like ___ than anyone else.
alts.why: An annoyed reaction, then a soft ending that contradicts it. That change of heart is what sounds fourteen.

segs.t: Ha — everyone says my dad, and it's so annoying.

wrong.t: I am most similar to my father.
wrong.why: That's the answer, stated stiffly. The reaction is how you feel about it.

wrong.t: That is an interesting question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: We've got the same laugh, the same terrible jokes and the same obsession with Marítimo.
Mind you, if I'm honest, I'd rather be like him than anyone else.

wrong.t: Mind you, he also supports Marítimo.
wrong.why: That's another similarity. 'Mind you' should turn the answer.

wrong.t: On the other hand, my mother is also nice.
wrong.why: Changes the subject instead of turning the feeling.

alts.frame: Hmm, probably my ___, actually. She ___ when I was little, and she taught me ___ before I could even ___. We're both quite ___, but we ___.
alts.why: A hesitation, a surprising answer, a detail with a comparison in it. The reason is about character, not appearance.

segs.t: Hmm, probably my grandma, actually.

wrong.t: Definitely, one hundred per cent, my grandma!
wrong.why: Too certain for a surprising answer. 'Probably… actually' sounds like you're thinking.

wrong.t: Well, that's a good question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: She moved in with us when I was little, and she taught me to cook before I could even ride a bike.
We're both quite quiet, but we notice everything. My family calls us 'the detectives'.

wrong.t: She taught me to cook when I was young.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: Grandparents play an important role in Portuguese families.
wrong.why: A sociology point. Why are YOU like her?

cards.question: Do you go on holiday with your family?

alts.frame: Yes, but we usually stay on the island. Last summer we spent ___ in ___ and ___ every day. We don't go abroad very often, because ___.
alts.why: Answer, one real holiday, then the honest 'but'. That's the shape of your B2 column, without the stray 'here's.

segs.t: Yes, but we usually stay on the island.
Last summer we spent a week in Porto Moniz and swam in the natural pools every day.

wrong.t: For example, we go on holiday in Madeira.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: Porto Moniz is in the north-west of the island.
wrong.why: Geography, not a memory.

segs.t: We don't go abroad very often, because flights from here are so expensive.

wrong.t: We also go to the beach a lot.
wrong.why: Adds, doesn't turn.

wrong.t: Nevertheless, domestic tourism has several advantages.
wrong.why: Correct English, but it sounds like a letter to the council. Part 1 is a chat — sound like you.

alts.frame: Not as much as I'd like to! My parents both work in ___, so ___ is their busiest time. So we go away in ___ instead — which sounds weird, but at least ___.
alts.why: 'Not as much as I'd like' is a reaction and an answer in one. The 'weird, but' ending turns a complaint into something good.

segs.t: Not as much as I'd like to!

wrong.t: No.
wrong.why: A closed door. React with the feeling behind it.

wrong.t: Holidays are important for families.
wrong.why: A general statement, not a reaction.

segs.t: My parents both work in hotels, so summer is their busiest time.
So we go away in November instead — which sounds weird, but at least the beaches in Porto Santo are completely empty.

wrong.t: So we don't go on holiday in summer.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: However, the hotel industry is essential to Madeira's economy.
wrong.why: True, but now you're writing an essay about tourism.

alts.frame: Yeah, every ___ we fly to ___ to see ___. It's the only time the whole family is together, so it's ___ but ___. Last year ___, and ___!
alts.why: Reason plus a funny example. The example does the proving — you don't need to say 'it's chaotic', you show it.

segs.t: Yeah, every August we fly to Lisbon to see my cousins.
It's the only time the whole family is together, so it's chaotic but amazing.

wrong.t: We go to Lisbon because my cousins live in Lisbon.
wrong.why: Circular — it repeats the answer.

wrong.t: Lisbon is a beautiful and historic city.
wrong.why: About Lisbon, not about why the trip matters.

segs.t: Last year there were fourteen of us in one flat, and we had to take turns in the shower!

wrong.t: For example, we visit lots of places in Lisbon.
wrong.why: Vague. One moment you could film.

wrong.t: My cousins are the same age as me.
wrong.why: A fact, not a moment.

cards.question: Who do you spend time with at the weekend?

alts.frame: My ___, mostly — it's a very Madeiran thing! Every Sunday we have ___ at ___. It can get a bit ___, to be honest, but I'd really miss it if ___.
alts.why: A reaction with a smile, a fact, then a mixed feeling. 'I'd miss it if we stopped' is a second conditional doing emotional work.

segs.t: My family, mostly — it's a very Madeiran thing!

wrong.t: I spend time with my family here at weekends.
wrong.why: Your table's version — but the stray 'here' is a habit to avoid, and it's the answer, not a reaction.

wrong.t: That is an interesting question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: Every Sunday we have a massive lunch at my grandparents' house in Câmara de Lobos.
It can get a bit boring, to be honest, but I'd really miss it if we stopped.

wrong.t: It's also really delicious and fun.
wrong.why: No turn. Where's the other side?

wrong.t: However, some teenagers prefer to spend time with friends.
wrong.why: About 'some teenagers', not you.

alts.frame: My friends, definitely. On ___ we meet at ___ and just ___ for hours. It sounds pointless, but it's the only time we can ___. Last Saturday we ___ and bought absolutely nothing.
alts.why: 'It sounds pointless, but…' defends your answer before the examiner can judge it. The example is a punchline.

segs.t: My friends, definitely. On Saturdays we meet at Forum Madeira and just walk around for hours.
It sounds pointless, but it's the only time we can talk without our parents listening.

wrong.t: We go to Forum Madeira because it's a shopping centre.
wrong.why: Obvious. Why do you go?

wrong.t: Shopping centres are popular places for young people.
wrong.why: A general fact, not your reason.

segs.t: Last Saturday we spent three hours there and bought absolutely nothing.

wrong.t: For example, there are many shops there.
wrong.why: About the place, not about a Saturday.

wrong.t: We like shopping very much.
wrong.why: A feeling, not a moment.

alts.frame: It depends on the weekend. Every other Saturday I stay with my ___ in ___, because ___. It used to feel strange, but now I actually like ___!
alts.why: 'Used to… but now' tells a change in one breath. Serious content, light ending — that's complex without being heavy.

segs.t: It depends on the weekend.

wrong.t: I spend time with different people.
wrong.why: Vague, and it isn't a reaction. 'It depends' buys time naturally.

wrong.t: Well, that's a good question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: Every other Saturday I stay with my dad in Machico, because my parents are separated.
It used to feel strange, but now I actually like having two homes — double the birthday presents!

wrong.t: It is strange to have two homes.
wrong.why: Stops at the hard part. The 'but now' is what shows how you feel today.

wrong.t: Divorce is increasingly common in modern society.
wrong.why: An essay sentence. Keep it about you.

cards.question: What's your city like?

alts.frame: Honestly? It's ___, but it's never ___. ___'s squeezed between ___ and ___, so wherever you go, ___. The only thing is, in ___ the centre gets packed with ___.
alts.why: A quick opinion, a picture, then the downside. Three moves, three different jobs.

segs.t: Honestly? It's small, but it's never boring.

wrong.t: My city is a city in Madeira.
wrong.why: Flat. A reaction shows how the question makes you feel.

wrong.t: That is an interesting question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: Funchal's squeezed between the mountains and the sea, so wherever you go, you've got an amazing view.
The only thing is, in summer the centre gets packed with tourists, and walking anywhere takes ages.

wrong.t: Also, there are many beautiful gardens.
wrong.why: No turn. A contrast has to swing back the other way.

wrong.t: However, tourism has both advantages and disadvantages.
wrong.why: Correct English, but it sounds like a letter to the council. Part 1 is a chat — sound like you.

alts.frame: It's pretty ___, to be honest — I live in ___, not ___. It's right next to ___, but you stop noticing after a while. Mind you, when ___, half the town ___!
alts.why: No reaction, straight in. The reason explains the noise; the example turns an annoyance into a local show.

segs.t: It's pretty quiet, to be honest — I live in Machico, not Funchal.
It's right next to the airport, but you stop noticing after a while.
marks: you stop noticing after a while

wrong.t: Machico is a quiet town in the east.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: Airports are important for islands.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

segs.t: Mind you, when it's windy and the planes can't land, half the town goes out to watch!

wrong.t: For example, many planes land there.
wrong.why: Vague. An example is one moment you could film — a day, a place, a person.

wrong.t: Madeira airport has a famous runway.
wrong.why: A fact from a guidebook, not something from your life.

alts.frame: Oh, I love it, but I'm biased! ___ feels like a big city and a village at the same time. Like, you can ___ in the evening, and the next morning ___.
alts.why: One clever idea — city and village at once — proved by one tiny scene.

segs.t: Oh, I love it, but I'm biased!

wrong.t: I think it's nice.
wrong.why: Flat. A reaction shows how the question makes you feel.

wrong.t: Well, that's a good question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: Funchal feels like a big city and a village at the same time.
Like, you can go to a concert in the evening, and the next morning the man at the bakery asks you how it was.

wrong.t: For example, there are many shops and cafés.
wrong.why: Vague. An example is one moment you could film — a day, a place, a person.

wrong.t: Funchal has about 100,000 people.
wrong.why: A fact from a guidebook, not something from your life.

cards.question: Where's the best place to go with friends in your city?

alts.frame: Definitely ___. It's ___ right by ___. It's cheap, it's ___, and there's always ___. Last summer we went almost every day, and we'd stay until ___.
alts.why: Answer, three quick reasons in one breath, then a memory that proves it.

segs.t: Definitely the Lido. It's a big outdoor pool right by the sea.
It's cheap, it's close to the centre, and there's always someone from school there.

wrong.t: The Lido is a swimming pool in Funchal.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: Swimming is good exercise for teenagers.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

segs.t: Last summer we went almost every day, and we'd stay until they literally closed the gates.

wrong.t: For example, we go there a lot.
wrong.why: Vague. An example is one moment you could film — a day, a place, a person.

wrong.t: The Lido was renovated a few years ago.
wrong.why: A fact from a guidebook, not something from your life.

alts.frame: Ha — anywhere with free Wi-Fi! No, seriously, we usually end up at ___. It's not exactly ___, but it's ___, and nobody ___.
alts.why: A joke first, then 'No, seriously' — the move that turns a joke into a real answer.

segs.t: Ha — anywhere with free Wi-Fi!

wrong.t: The best place is a shopping centre.
wrong.why: That's the answer, and it skips the fun. React first.

wrong.t: That is an interesting question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: No, seriously, we usually end up at Forum Madeira, in the food court.
It's not exactly exciting, but it's warm when it rains, the chips are cheap, and nobody tells us to leave.

wrong.t: It's also very big and modern.
wrong.why: No turn. A contrast has to swing back the other way.

wrong.t: However, shopping centres are bad for local shops.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

alts.frame: The ___, especially ___. We sit on ___ and just talk for hours. Last Friday we ___ and made up funny stories about ___.
alts.why: No reaction, no reason: the place and one evening there. Sometimes two moves are enough.

segs.t: The seafront, especially around sunset. We sit on the wall by the marina and just talk for hours.
Last Friday we watched a huge cruise ship leave and made up funny stories about all the passengers on board.

wrong.t: For example, the seafront is very beautiful.
wrong.why: Vague. An example is one moment you could film — a day, a place, a person.

wrong.t: Many cruise ships visit Funchal every year.
wrong.why: A fact from a guidebook, not something from your life.

cards.question: Is there anything you'd change about your city?

alts.frame: Yes, I'd definitely improve ___. They're often ___, and ___ is so ___ that ___ isn't really an option. Last week I waited ___ and missed ___.
alts.why: Answer, reason, and a small disaster as proof. The second conditional ('I'd') is doing the work.

segs.t: Yes, I'd definitely improve the buses.
They're often late, and some of the hills are so steep that walking isn't really an option.

wrong.t: The buses need to be better.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: Public transport is essential in modern cities.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

segs.t: Last week I waited forty minutes in São Martinho and missed the start of my Maths test.

wrong.t: For example, buses are sometimes late.
wrong.why: That's the reason again. One day, one bus, one consequence.

wrong.t: The buses in Funchal are yellow.
wrong.why: A fact from a guidebook, not something from your life.

alts.frame: Hmm, just one thing, really. I'd make more places for ___, like ___. At the moment there's loads for ___, but if you're ___, there's not much to do ___.
alts.why: 'At the moment… but if you're fourteen' — the contrast is between two groups of people, and you're in one of them.

segs.t: Hmm, just one thing, really.

wrong.t: Yes, I would change many things.
wrong.why: Not a reaction, and it promises a list you won't give.

wrong.t: Well, that's a good question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: I'd make more places for teenagers, like a skate park or a youth club.
At the moment there's loads for tourists, but if you're fourteen, there's not much to do in the evenings.

wrong.t: Also, I'd like more cinemas.
wrong.why: No turn. A contrast has to swing back the other way.

wrong.t: Nevertheless, the city offers many facilities.
wrong.why: Correct English, but it sounds like a letter to the council. Part 1 is a chat — sound like you.

alts.frame: Honestly? Not much. I'd just ___ at weekends. It's the prettiest part of ___, with ___, but it's impossible to enjoy it properly with ___.
alts.why: 'Not much' — then one precise change. A small, specific answer sounds more confident than a long list.

segs.t: Honestly? Not much.

wrong.t: My city is perfect.
wrong.why: Closes the door. 'Not much' leaves room for one idea.

wrong.t: That is an interesting question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: I'd just ban cars from the old town at weekends.
It's the prettiest part of Funchal, with all the painted doors and little cafés, but it's impossible to enjoy it properly with traffic everywhere.

wrong.t: I'd ban cars because I don't like cars.
wrong.why: Circular. Why the old town?

wrong.t: Cars cause pollution in many cities.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

cards.question: Do you travel far every day?

alts.frame: Not really, I'm lucky! I take ___ to my school in ___, and it only takes about ___. Although in the morning it's so ___ that I usually have to ___.
alts.why: 'I'm lucky' is a reaction with a smile. 'Although… so packed that' turns it around neatly.

segs.t: Not really, I'm lucky!

wrong.t: No, I don't travel far.
wrong.why: The answer, not a reaction. How do you feel about it?

wrong.t: That is an interesting question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: I take the bus to my school in the centre, and it only takes about twenty-five minutes.
Although in the morning it's so packed that I usually have to stand the whole way.

wrong.t: Although the bus is quite comfortable.
wrong.why: No turn. A contrast has to swing back the other way.

wrong.t: However, traffic is a problem in many cities.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

alts.frame: Yeah, quite far, actually — I live in ___, and my school's in ___. My parents wanted me to go to a school with ___, so I don't really mind. Mind you, last week I ___!
alts.why: A long journey needs a reason, and the example makes it funny instead of a complaint.

segs.t: Yeah, quite far, actually — I live in Camacha, and my school's in Funchal.
My parents wanted me to go to a school with a good music programme, so I don't really mind.

wrong.t: It's far because Camacha is far from Funchal.
wrong.why: Circular — the geography isn't a reason.

wrong.t: Many students travel long distances to school.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

segs.t: Mind you, last week I fell asleep on the bus and woke up at the very last stop!

wrong.t: For example, the bus takes fifty minutes.
wrong.why: Vague. An example is one moment you could film — a day, a place, a person.

wrong.t: Camacha is famous for wicker baskets.
wrong.why: A fact from a guidebook, not something from your life.

alts.frame: Oh, no — I'm really lucky. I just walk. My school's only about ___ from my flat. The only problem is that it's all ___, so I arrive every morning looking like ___.
alts.why: Short journey, short answer — and a funny image at the end so it doesn't die.

segs.t: Oh, no — I'm really lucky.

wrong.t: No.
wrong.why: A closed door. Show a feeling.

wrong.t: Well, that's a good question.
wrong.why: The examiner hears this fifty times a day. It fills the silence without saying anything about you.

segs.t: I just walk. My school's only about ten minutes from my flat.
The only problem is that it's all uphill, so I arrive every morning looking like I've run a marathon.

wrong.t: And the walk is really nice.
wrong.why: No turn. A contrast has to swing back the other way.

wrong.t: However, walking is healthier than driving.
wrong.why: About people in general, not about you. Keep it personal.

cards.question: Do you prefer going by car or by public transport?

alts.frame: I definitely prefer ___. The bus is ___ and ___, and I can ___ on the way. The only downside is that it's sometimes ___, especially when ___.
alts.why: Your B2 answer, cleaned up: answer, two reasons joined naturally, and an honest downside.

segs.t: I definitely prefer public transport.
The bus is cheaper and better for the environment, and I can chat to my friends on the way.

wrong.t: I prefer the bus to the car.
wrong.why: That's the answer again in different words. This move has to add something new.

wrong.t: Public transport reduces carbon emissions significantly.
wrong.why: Correct English, but it sounds like a letter to the council. Part 1 is a chat — sound like you.

segs.t: The only downside is that it's sometimes late, especially when it's windy along the coast.

wrong.t: Also, the bus drivers are friendly.
wrong.why: No turn. A contrast has to swing back the other way.
